english: Let $A$ and $B$ be $3\times3$ matrices with real entries such that $\mathrm{tr}\left(A^{2}\right)=2$, $\mathrm{tr}\left(B^{2}\right)=4$ and $\mathrm{tr}\left((A+2B)^{2}\right)=4$, where $\mathrm{tr}(X)$ denotes the trace of a square matrix $X$. Then the value of $\mathrm{tr}\left((2A-B)(A+B)\right)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $A$ तथा $B$ वास्तविक प्रविष्टियों वाले $3\times3$ आव्यूह हैं जिनके लिए $\mathrm{tr}\left(A^{2}\right)=2$, $\mathrm{tr}\left(B^{2}\right)=4$ तथा $\mathrm{tr}\left((A+2B)^{2}\right)=4$ है, जहाँ $\mathrm{tr}(X)$ वर्ग आव्यूह $X$ का अनुरेख (trace) है। तब $\mathrm{tr}\left((2A-B)(A+B)\right)$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Matrix multiplication is not commutative, so $(A+2B)^{2}=(A+2B)(A+2B)=A^{2}+2AB+2BA+4B^{2}$, keeping $AB$ and $BA$ separate.
The trace is linear, and $\mathrm{tr}(XY)=\mathrm{tr}(YX)$ for square matrices: $\mathrm{tr}(XY)=\sum_{i,j}x_{ij}y_{ji}=\mathrm{tr}(YX)$. So $\mathrm{tr}(BA)=\mathrm{tr}(AB)$; call it $t$.
Such matrices exist, e.g. $A=\mathrm{diag}(1,1,0)$ and $B=\begin{pmatrix}-\frac54&\frac14&0\\-\frac14&-\frac54&0\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$, so the data are consistent.
originality_note: New: only traces of squares are given for two non-commuting matrices, and the trace of a different mixed product is asked; the cross terms combine only because tr(AB) = tr(BA) (way 4, a hidden invariant). Closest known: questions giving A + 2B and 2A - B explicitly and asking tr. Different because: no matrix is given and the non-commutative expansion must be kept.
blueprint_concepts: Trace Properties: Tr(AB) = Tr(BA), trace of symmetric/skew-symmetric matrices.

concept_use.Trace Properties: Tr(AB) = Tr(BA), trace: tr(AB) = tr(BA) lets both cross terms combine into t, found from tr((A+2B)^2) = 4 and then used in tr((2A-B)(A+B)).

stem_review: Read as a student: every matrix and symbol is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked: sympy verifies the data and the value -7/2 for the explicit pair A = diag(1,1,0) and B given in the full solution; -3.50 is a negative decimal as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: Expanding (A+2B)^2 without commuting and using tr(AB) = tr(BA) to get tr(AB) = -7/2.
